# Sinsy — vendored data

This folder holds the assets the Japanese chain needs at runtime, so that the installed
package is self-contained for Japanese and does not require a separate download.

```text
LICENSE-sinsy.txt                     upstream LICENSE.txt (hts_engine API + Sinsy)
dic/japanese.utf_8.{conf,table}       phoneme tables, UTF-8      <- the one we use
dic/japanese.euc_jp.{conf,table}      phoneme tables, EUC-JP     (kept for parity)
dic/japanese.shift_jis.{conf,table}   phoneme tables, Shift-JIS  (kept for parity)
voice/nitech_jp_song070_f001.htsvoice  HTS Voice "NIT SONG070 F001" 0.90
voice/COPYING                         the model's own notice (CC BY 3.0)
voice/README                          the model's own README (title, licence, credits)
voice/INSTALL                         the model's own INSTALL
```

## Where it came from

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Sinsy | version 0.92, released 2015-12-25, <http://sinsy.sourceforge.net/> |
| `dic/` | copied verbatim from the Sinsy 0.92 source tree |
| `LICENSE-sinsy.txt` | copied verbatim from the Sinsy 0.92 source tree |
| voice model | `hts_voice_nitech_jp_song070_f001-0.90.tar.gz`, the official distribution of HTS Voice "NIT SONG070 F001" version 0.90 (2013-12-25) |
| `voice/COPYING`, `voice/README`, `voice/INSTALL` | copied unmodified from that archive |
| model SHA-256 | `25253E329DF090E0452C8F63D660346B3B1BDC27F429E1958A5162DDE018F7B2` |

## Why it is here and not built

`dic/` is data read at runtime; the model is a trained acoustic model. Neither is
generated by the build, so they live in the repository and are copied into the package
by the csproj (`sinsy/dic/*`, `sinsy/voice/*`).

## Licence — two different ones

- **Sinsy code and phoneme tables**: Modified BSD (3-clause), Nagoya Institute of
  Technology. See `LICENSE-sinsy.txt`.
- **The voice model**: **Creative Commons Attribution 3.0**
  (<https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/>), Copyright (c) 2009-2013 Nagoya
  Institute of Technology, Department of Computer Science, released by the Sinsy Working
  Group. Trained on the Nitech Japanese Speech Database "NIT SONG070 F001"
  (Copyright (c) 2004-2013, HTS Working Group, also CC BY 3.0). See `voice/COPYING`.

Under CC BY we must name the work, credit the licensor and state the licence — which is
what `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` and the package's introduction do.

## What we do *not* use it for

The model produces phoneme durations and F0 only. Its own spectral envelope and
aperiodicity are never used: the timbre of a rendered voice comes from the MUTA voice
bank the user has installed. This is why a MUTA voice can sing Japanese at all.
